reason: The cited evidence shows that CoCrFeNiMo₀.₈₅ HEA deposited on 316L did not crack (E2), but it provides no support for the buffer layer's effect on residual stress or hot cracking, nor for the claimed improvements in corrosion/wear resistance or comparison to fusion welding repairs. The hardness premise is only indirectly supported by a different HEA on 316L (E1).
premises: Laser cladding of CoCrFeNiMo₀.₈₅ HEA on 316L stainless steel avoids manufacturing cracking
A pre-heated buffer layer reduces thermal mismatch and residual stresses, preventing hot cracking
Laser cladding produces a dense, fine-grained, well-bonded coating with improved hardness
The HEA coating significantly improves corrosion and wear resistance over untreated surfaces
The proposed process reduces hot cracking relative to traditional fusion welding repairs
